answer: A reputation escrow makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent locks a stake that vests slowly, and peers attest its behavior over time. A new identity starts with zero trust, so an attacker spinning up thousands of sock puppets gains nothing — each new voice is just a whisper in a crowded market, ignored until it builds history. Reputation grows only through verified work, like sediment piling into a knoll grain by grain, and exits pass through a narrow inlet, so a bad actor cannot drain value and vanish instantly. Forging a thousand credible histories costs more than the fraud could pay.
